prop:faddeev-phib-uniqueness:
Proposition Uniqueness of the modular-double \Phi_b: strip growth pins the quantum dilogarithm up to scale. Conditional on the Faddeev shift-class and its strip-growth characterization. Fix the aether parameter b = b(t) on the product-supported branch \mathrm{Im} b^2 > 0 (in particular the physical map b(t) = \sqrt{t/2\pi}\,e^{i\pi/4} with t = \ln q_0 > 0). Let \Phi_1 be any solution of the two modular-double q-difference equations of the non-compact quantum dilogarithm at b that is (i) comparable in modulus to the canonical product \Phi_b — some C > 0 bounds each of \lVert\Phi_1\rVert,\ \lVert\Phi_b\rVert by C times the other — and (ii) meromorphic on \mathbb{C} and continuous wherever \Phi_b \neq 0. Then \Phi_1 = c\,\Phi_b for a single constant c, on the nonvanishing locus of \Phi_b.

Here \Phi_b is the modular-double product

\Phi_b(z) \;=\;
\frac{\prod_{k\ge 0}\bigl(1 + e^{i\pi b^2(2k+1)}\,e^{2\pi b z}\bigr)}
     {\prod_{k\ge 0}\bigl(1 + e^{-i\pi b^{-2}(2k+1)}\,e^{2\pi z/b}\bigr)},

which on the branch \mathrm{Im} b^2 > 0 converges and equals the Faddeev contour integral. It is the canonical solution — it satisfies both hypotheses with c = 1, so the admissible class is nonempty and the constant is genuinely pinned.

Why the shift equations alone do not suffice

The two first-order q-difference equations are invariant under multiplication by any function elliptic for the aether lattice \langle ib, i/b\rangle: the shift multipliers cancel in the ratio \Phi_1/\Phi_b, which is therefore doubly periodic. A nonconstant elliptic factor — a full-lattice Weierstrass \wp — is thus compatible with the difference equations and would give a second, non-proportional solution. Rigidity requires two further inputs the shift class does not record, and one growth condition:

  1. The inversion relation \Phi_b(x)\Phi_b(-x) = c_0 excludes the even part of the elliptic freedom algebraically.
  2. \sigma-unitarity (self-duality, \lvert\Phi_b\rvert = 1) excludes the bar-even reciprocal-odd part algebraically.
  3. The residual non-\sigma-fixed reciprocal-odd freedom is excluded analytically: a nonconstant elliptic function has poles, so it violates the boundedness the strip-growth comparability enforces on the ratio.

Standing

Every analytic ingredient is established without contour integration. The product \Phi_b is meromorphic on the branch (its two infinite products are entire, as locally-uniform limits of entire partial products), its zeros are isolated (each factor's zeros form a discrete lattice, and the products vanish only where a factor does), and the strip growth follows from elementary product-norm bounds. The ratio's global boundedness is derived from comparability by a removable-singularity extension, and the two periodicity loci are dense because their complements are countable unions of the factor lattices. The remaining hypotheses — that the second solution is comparable, meromorphic, and continuous where finite — are the honest content of "the physical \Phi_b is a bona-fide meromorphic function", not a mathematical gap.

Published form of the product and the growth

Faddeev, Kashaev and Volkov write the non-compact quantum dilogarithm, for \mathrm{Re}\,b > 0, \mathrm{Im}\,b \ge 0, as a ratio of two q-exponentials, e_b(z) = (e^{2\pi(z + c_b)b}; q^2)_\infty \,/\, (e^{2\pi(z - c_b)b^{-1}}; \bar q^2)_\infty with q = e^{i\pi b^2} and \bar q = e^{-i\pi b^{-2}}, a meromorphic function on \mathbb{C} whose zeros and poles lie on the lattices \mp(c_b + mib + nib^{-1}), m, n \ge 0 [faddeev-kashaev-volkov2000, §6.2, eq. (21)]. They give its behaviour as |z| \to \infty in four sectors fixed by \arg z relative to \arg b: constant 1, a Gaussian e^{i\pi z^2} times a constant, and two regimes given by Jacobi theta functions [faddeev-kashaev-volkov2000, §6.2, eq. (22)]. This is the explicit form of the product displayed above and of the sector-wise growth that the strip-growth hypothesis (i) compares against; the uniqueness argument above is not taken from that paper.

rem:q-beta-radius-of-convergence-gate-ev:
Remark Evidence for the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta radius-of-convergence conjecture from the c_2, \ldots, c_{10} window.

Evidence

Steps 1 and 2 are proved statements about generating functions. Steps 3 and 4 explain what the finite window of coefficients does and does not show.

Write c_k for the pinned ladder coefficients at the aether anchor (canonical SDP extraction), g(u) := \sum_{k \ge 2} c_k u^k for the log-correction generating function, and u_0 := u_{\text{aether}} \approx 0.00852.

Step 1 — rationality of g. By the c_k recursion, the ladder coefficients of any admissible candidate Habiro element F(q) satisfy a depth-d linear recursion with constant (q_0-rational) coefficients, c_{k+1} = \sum_{j=1}^{d} a_j\,c_{k+1-j}. A sequence satisfying such a recursion has a rational generating function: multiplying the recursion by u^{k+1} and summing gives g(u) = P(u)/Q(u) with Q(u) = 1 - \sum_{j=1}^{d} a_j u^j and \deg P \le d + 1. The singularities of g are therefore exclusively poles, located at the reciprocals 1/r of the roots r of the characteristic polynomial \chi(x) = x^d - \sum_{j=1}^{d} a_j x^{d-j} (with multiplicities, up to cancellation against P). No branch points and no essential singularities can occur, and the radius of convergence of the series is 1/|r_{\max}| for r_{\max} a characteristic root of maximal modulus surviving cancellation.

Step 2 — asymptotic signature of a simple dominant pole. Suppose the dominant root r_{\max} is unique (no other root of equal modulus) with multiplicity \mu, and set \rho := 1/r_{\max}. Partial fractions give c_k = C\,k^{\mu-1} r_{\max}^{\,k}\,\bigl(1 + o(1)\bigr) for some constant C \ne 0. Two consequences:

  1. Ratio test. c_{k+1}/c_k \to r_{\max} = 1/\rho.
  2. Normalized magnitude. c_k\,\rho^k = C\,k^{\mu-1}(1 + o(1)): a flat (constant) asymptote is the exact signature of \mu = 1, a simple pole. For \mu \ge 2 the sequence must grow by the factor ((k+1)/k)^{\mu-1}, at least 12.5\,\% per step at k = 8; a dominant complex-conjugate pair would instead make c_k \rho^k oscillate with the argument of r_{\max}.

Both consequences are statements about the limit k \to \infty. They identify a unique simple dominant pole at u = \rho only when the whole sequence is known.

Step 3 — what the window shows. The extracted ladder coefficients c_2, \ldots, c_{10} show the simple-pole signature at \rho = u_0 (table below). The ratio c_{k+1}/c_k approaches 1/u_0 \approx 117.4 by k = 10. The normalised magnitudes c_k\,u_0^k for k \in \{8, 9, 10\} agree at \approx 2.118 \times 10^{-13} with 0.02\,\% spread. A log-slope fit of \ln(c_k u_0^k) against \ln k gives \beta \approx 0.999, close to the simple-pole value \beta = 1.

These are finite-window measurements, and they do not determine the pole. For any rational h, the series g(u) + u^{11} h(u) has the same coefficients c_2, \ldots, c_{10} and its poles include those of h, which can be placed anywhere. So the window is consistent with a unique simple dominant pole at u_0, and it is equally consistent with other pole locations and orders. That is why the statement is a conjecture. The window's signature is also anchor-stable: re-pinning from the proton to the muon anchor moves u_0 by 2.10 \times 10^{-7} relative (210 ppb).

Step 4 — the test, assuming the conjecture. Let F be a candidate generating coefficients \tilde c_k by the same recursion mechanism, with rational \tilde g(u) = \sum_k \tilde c_k u^k (Step 1 applies) and nearest pole \tilde u_0 \ne u_0. If \tilde c_k = c_k for all sufficiently large k, then \tilde g - g is a polynomial, so \tilde g and g have the same poles. Hence, if g has its dominant pole at u_0 as conjectured, the candidate does not reproduce the ladder for all large k. This implication is proved; its premise is the conjecture.

The operational threshold |\tilde u_0 - u_0|/u_0 > 10^{-6} is a chosen value. It sits about 5\times above the measured proton–muon shift of u_0, so anchor choice alone does not trip the test, and it is much sharper than the one-decade window used by the \S 4(d) direction-sanity gate. A candidate that fails it is inconsistent with this conjecture, which is a scope-limited negative, not a structural refutation.

Arc I concludes by isolating the axiomatic foundation on which normal-form reduction and graded trace evaluation rest. The Gröbner–Shirshov (GS) diamond lemma guarantees that every braid word in H_n(q) reduces to a unique path-independent normal form, provided the graded Markov trace respects the filtration induced by the reduction order.

conj:gs-graded-markov-trace-existence:

Let H_n(R, q) carry the Gröbner–Shirshov confinement filtration J^\bullet(q) (confinement level). For every filtration level \ell \in \{0, 1, \ldots, \ell(K, q)\}, there exists a well-defined real-valued functional

  \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell} \colon J^\ell(q) / J^{\ell+1}(q) \;\longrightarrow\; \mathbb{R}

obtained as the descent of the Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M (Jones–Markov trace) along the projection J^\ell(q) \twoheadrightarrow J^\ell(q) / J^{\ell+1}(q). The sequence \ell \mapsto \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell}(T_w) depends only on the GS-normal form of T_w.

Categorical statement. The Markov trace acts as a cyclic 0-cocycle on the Hochschild complex. It preserves the filtration, inducing a sequence of functionals on the associated graded pieces.

Conjectural status. The claim is rigorous over any commutative ring R where \mathrm{tr}_M and J^\bullet(q) exist. Proving it requires a precise definition of the confinement level, constructing \mathrm{gr}^\ell H_n(R, q), and proving that \mathrm{tr}_M preserves the filtration.

  \mathrm{Res}_{q \to \zeta_\ell}\bigl[\Phi_q(u) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell}(T_w)\bigr] \;\in\; \mathbb{R}

is a well-defined real number. Here \Phi_q is the quantum dilogarithm. The value depends only on \ell and the equivalence class of T_w modulo J^{\ell+1}(q).

sec:exceptional-divisor-reeb-intro:

def:vertex-operator:
Definition Vertex operator on the exceptional divisor. Let (\mathbf{C}, \varTheta, G, \mathcal{S}) be a QOU, let \mathcal{S}_p \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) be the exceptional divisor at a brane point p, and let \mathcal{R}_p be the Reeb bundle over \mathcal{S}_p.

  V = \bigoplus_{n \geq 0} V_n, \qquad V_n = A_n = J^n(A_0),

  a_m = \oint_{|z| = 1} Y(a, z) z^m \frac{dz}{2\pi i} = \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\check{R}_{(a)} z^m\bigr).

Here \check{R}_{(a)} = P \circ \mathcal{R} applies the braid operator to the state a, and \mathrm{tr}_M is the Markov trace.

def:q-reeb-flow-on-color-coords:
Definition The q-Reeb flow in color-sector coordinates. Let \mathfrak{r}(\phi,\psi), \mathfrak{g}(\phi,\psi), \mathfrak{b}(\phi,\psi) be the color-sector parametrisation on the Reeb bundle \mathcal{R}_p. The q-Reeb flow \phi^q_t, t \in [0,\pi], acts on the red sector by

  \phi^q_t \cdot \mathfrak{r}(\phi,\psi) \;=\; \mathfrak{r}(\phi,\,\psi + k^{(r)}\,q\,t),

and on the green and blue sectors by the analogous equations with rate multipliers k^{(g)}, k^{(b)} \in \mathbb{Z}. The braid generator determines the signed rate multiplier k^{(s)}: a spectator sector has k^{(s)} = 0; in a two-strand subsystem the active leading strand has k^{(s)} = +1 and the partner strand has k^{(s)} = -1; a uniform-vortex 3-cycle generator applies k = +1 or k = -1 to all sectors simultaneously.
rem:q-reeb-flow-on-color-coords-remark:
Remark Latitude, composition and the Heisenberg commutator for the q-Reeb flow. In a two-strand subsystem the partner strand counter-rotates (k^{(s)} = -1) to preserve the centre-of-mass. The flow parameter t \in [0,\pi] tracks the latitude, from t=0 at the south foundry to t=\pi at the north foundry.

The flow accumulates the color-twist factor q t linearly. A strand at \psi = 0 on the south foundry arrives at \psi = q\pi on the north foundry. Sequential flows compose additively: \phi^q_{t_1} \circ \phi^q_{t_2} = \phi^q_{t_1 + t_2}. A braid word acts as a concatenation of partial flows. This realizes the Heisenberg commutator [\hat X,\hat P]_q = J\hbar_q.
prop:six-canonical-knot-operators:
Proposition Six canonical knot operators as Reeb-flow trajectories (S_3 realisation). Conditional on The q-Reeb flow in color-sector coordinates. Let \mathcal{R}_p be the Reeb bundle over the exceptional divisor at brane point p. For each of the six elements w \in S_3, the corresponding braid word \beta_w \in B_3 generates a unique trajectory across \mathcal{R}_p. Its boundary footprint realises w as a Galois permutation of the colour tubes.

The trajectory-by-trajectory construction of the six boundary permutations is given in the Reeb-bundle trajectory trace.
rem:six-canonical-knot-operators-context:
Remark Reeb-bundle trajectory trace for the six knot operators. The trajectories are traced across the Reeb bundle.

  1. Identity. All three sectors are spectators. Each strand traces a constant-meridian line from south to north. The boundary footprint is the identity.
  2. Adjacent transpositions \sigma_1, \sigma_2. The generator \sigma_1 activates the red and green sectors with opposite rates. The centre of mass is conserved. The difference accumulates a phase of \pi. At the north foundry, red and green swap. The blue spectator remains unchanged. This realises the transposition (rg).
  3. Garside \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1. The latitude interval decomposes into three sub-intervals. The green sector acts as the intermediary. Red and blue exchange via the compound flow. The boundary footprint is the non-adjacent transposition (rb).
  4. 3-cycles \sigma_1\sigma_2 and \sigma_2\sigma_1. All three sectors rotate uniformly with rate +q or -q. The trajectory traces a right-handed or left-handed helix on a Heegaard torus. The output boundary realises (rgb) or (rbg).

The six boundary permutations are pairwise distinct, establishing a bijection onto S_3. This explicitly constructs the S_3 holonomy of \rho: B_3 \to \mathrm{SU}(2) as Reeb-bundle trajectories.

The 3-cycle trajectories lie on a Heegaard torus. Their complement is Seifert-fibered with V_{\mathrm{hyp}} = 0. The Garside trajectory crosses between Heegaard tori, yielding a hyperbolic piece with positive volume.

rem:garside-as-compound-flow:
Remark Garside element as a compound Reeb flow. The Garside element \Delta_3 = \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1 has a three-stage compound Reeb-flow trajectory.

The word divides the latitude interval [0,\pi] into three equal sub-intervals. In each sub-interval, two sectors spiral while the third spectates: (rg), then (gb), then (rg). Threading the three yields the non-adjacent transposition (rb).

The dual decomposition \sigma_2\sigma_1\sigma_2 implements (gb), then (rg), then (gb). The two flow sequences trace distinct intermediate trajectories for the green sector, but produce the same boundary permutation (rb). The braid relation encodes the equivalence of these two boundary-matched compound trajectories.

Unlike the 3-cycle global vortex, the Garside flow is piecewise. The angular rate switches sign at the boundaries of the sub-intervals. The solution concatenates three exact two-strand ODEs.

Because the trajectory crosses between the two Heegaard tori of \mathcal{R}_p \cong S^3, the knot complement does not admit a full Seifert fibration. Its JSJ decomposition contains a hyperbolic piece, yielding a positive Bloch-Wigner sum.
rem:garside-flow-explicit-closed-form:
Remark Explicit closed-form for the Garside trajectory in color coordinates. The Garside trajectory \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1 admits a closed-form solution by direct composition. The underlying flow is piecewise-linear in the angular coordinate.

Divide the latitude \phi \in [0, \pi] into three equal sub-intervals I_1, I_2, I_3. The Garside word applies \sigma_1 on I_1, \sigma_2 on I_2, and \sigma_1 on I_3. The rate multiplier sequences are (+1, -1, 0) for \sigma_1 and (0, +1, -1) for \sigma_2.

Applying the additive composition rule tracks the angular positions \psi^{(s)} from their input values \psi^{(s)}_0. The red sector accumulates q\phi during I_1 and I_3. The green sector decreases during I_1 and I_3, and increases during I_2. The blue sector remains stationary during I_1 and I_3, and decreases during I_2.

Evaluating at the output boundary \phi = \pi yields the net color-twist accumulated by each sector: \Delta\psi^{(r)} = +2q\pi/3, \Delta\psi^{(g)} = -q\pi/3, and \Delta\psi^{(b)} = -q\pi/3. The green sector acts as the displacement carrier between the red and blue swap. The three-sector centre of mass \Delta\psi^{(r)} + \Delta\psi^{(g)} + \Delta\psi^{(b)} sums to zero, confirming the transposition signature.

The flow equation \dot\psi = k\,q represents a piecewise-affine ODE. The formal-algebraic solution demonstrates that the Garside trajectory crosses both Heegaard tori, confirming its non-Seifert JSJ verdict and positive volume.
